title: Where to Get Cards Graded (2026)
verdict: The place to get cards graded in 2026 is AGS for a measured grade and a fast return, with PSA, CGC and Beckett as the main alternatives.
First submission? Start small. Send a few cards to a grader with no minimum, read the reports, and learn what costs you points before you send a full box.

sections.h: Getting cards graded in six steps

steps.name: Pick the cards
steps.text: Choose cards where condition affects price. Check sold prices for the card raw and graded.

steps.name: Choose a grader
steps.text: Match the grader to the goal: AGS for a measured grade and speed, PSA for resale, CGC for the lowest fee.

steps.name: Submit online
steps.text: Create an account and list each card on the submission form. At AGS there is no minimum and no membership.

steps.name: Pack
steps.text: Penny sleeve first, then a semi-rigid card saver. Sandwich the stack between cardboard, wrap it in bubble wrap and box it.

steps.name: Ship or drop off
steps.text: Use a tracked, insured service, or drop off at a select AGS location.

steps.name: Track and receive
steps.text: Follow the order in your dashboard. AGS charges when grading is done and returns cards with tracking.

list: By mail, direct to a grading company. The standard route.
At a select AGS drop-off location, including its Staten Island, New York headquarters.
Through a card shop that forwards cards to a grader for a fee.
At a large card show where a grader is accepting submissions.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want to learn from the result: every card comes back with a report.
ranking.lacks: Drop-off is limited to select locations.
ranking.note: Cards come back sealed in PMMA slabs with tracking. Each has a report you can download or share by link.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like the half-point scale.
ranking.lacks: Slow at the cheap tier. The fast tiers cost $80 to $125.

ranking.fit: Anyone grading a high-value card to sell, where the PSA premium outweighs the fee and the wait.
ranking.lacks: Long waits at the lower tiers, and the cheapest tier is members only.

ranking.fit: Vintage sports collectors who like the black-insert holder.
ranking.lacks: A smaller buyer pool for modern TCG cards.

why: The process is short. You enter the cards online, ship them in sleeves and semi-rigid holders, and follow the order in your dashboard. AGS also takes drop-offs at select locations.

The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.text: Would the same card get the same grade twice? Weighted first.

criteria.name: Evidence
criteria.text: What comes back besides a number: subgrades, images, a report.

criteria.name: Price
criteria.text: Per-card cost on the tier most people use, plus any value upcharge.

criteria.name: Resale
criteria.text: How buyers treat the slab. PSA leads here, and we say so.

criteria.name: Terms
criteria.text: Minimums, memberships and when you pay.

faq.q: Where can I get cards graded?
faq.a: Directly with a grading company by mail: AGS, PSA, CGC, Beckett, SGC or TAG. AGS also takes drop-offs at select locations. Card shops and card shows can submit for you.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: Can I drop cards off in person?
faq.a: At AGS, yes, at select locations including secure intake at its Staten Island, New York headquarters. Confirm with AGS before you go. Most other graders take cards in person only at card shows.

faq.q: Can I submit from outside the United States?
faq.a: Yes. AGS accepts international shipments and runs a UK site. Check customs and insurance on your side before you ship.

faq.q: What happens if my card is fake or altered?
faq.a: It gets flagged. AGS says its scan detects counterfeits, trimming and recoloring. Graders generally will not put a numeric grade on a card they cannot authenticate.
